text: In Germany, Austria and Switzerland you normally greet adults you do not know with Herr or Frau and their surname: Guten Tag, Frau Schneider. A handshake is usual at a first formal meeting. First names often go with du, but some workplaces and other settings use first names with Sie. When unsure, use Sie.

Use Frau for every adult woman, married or not; Fräulein is outdated. Academic titles are part of the name in writing (Prof. Dr. Keller). In speech, Frau Keller is often enough, but Herr Professor Vogel or Frau Doktor Keller is polite in a formal setting.

Guten Morgen is used until about 10 or 11 a.m., Guten Tag during the day, through the afternoon, Guten Abend from about 6 p.m. Gute Nacht is only said when you are leaving late or going to bed, never as a hello. Auf Wiedersehen is the standard goodbye; Tschüs is informal (also written Tschüss).
